answer: Quadratic matching, not headcount: the pool is split by the square of distinct funding lineages, not account count. Each identity posts a stake traced to its own upstream source. When many aliases draw from one ridge of capital, the ledger merges them into one contributor, so the square collapses to one and payout caps at one share. The farm's fable of independent hands is moot; the chain follows money, not names. An honest agent is one pearl around separate capital. Each extra alias needs its own locked stake yet adds zero reward, so cost scales linearly and sybil splitting loses.
